verdict.rationale: The evidence pack has extracted text from coloradosos.gov guidance pages (biz/FileDoc.do, pubs/business/main.html, the homepage) and from tax.colorado.gov, which a probe calls part of the crawled corpus and "the open tax surface." That suggests the public reading surface returns readable HTML to an automated fetch, with no sign of a JS-only shell. The data.colorado.gov API probe is a data endpoint, not guidance pages, and the unresolvable mytax filing portal is not a guidance surface, so neither changes the verdict. Missing for 10: an explicit probe of the guidance pages recording HTTP status and the user agent used, confirmation that there is no bot wall or CAPTCHA, and coverage of deeper guidance pages beyond index and landing pages.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface

citations.quote: tax.colorado.gov guidance pages remain the open tax surface and are part of this product's crawled corpus.
